sections.h2: What are my choices for selling a house in Cedar Park?
sections.html:
Three paths exist in Cedar Park: hire an agent, run the sale yourself, or hand the keys to a buyer who pays cash for the house in its current state. The deciding factors are the shape the house is in and the date you need to be done.

  • Agent route: the most exposure to buyers, paired with showings, a lender's appraisal and repair requests after the inspection.
  • Do it yourself: you set the price and write the paperwork with a title company's help.
  • Cash, as-is: a fit for deferred repairs, a tenant, an estate or a short fuse.

Whatever you choose, three Cedar Park items come up in nearly every sale: the permit record, any short-term rental registration, and the tax account.

sections.h2: How did Cedar Park become the city it is today?
sections.html:
Cedar Park grew from a ranch settlement into an Austin suburb that was incorporated in 1973. The Texas Historical Commission marker in front of the public library tells it: in 1873 a couple bought a large tract rich in cedar and limestone, a post office opened in 1874 under the name Running Brushy, and the railroad arrived in 1882 when the name changed to Bruggerhoff. Five years later the present name was adopted.

The marker adds that the founder opened a cedar yard to sell posts as barbed wire spread, that little growth came in the first half of the twentieth century, and that by 1960 nearly all traces of the old community had disappeared. Austin's growth in the 1970s pulled people north. The city's economic development group now calls Cedar Park the third largest city in the Austin metro and a part of Williamson County.

sections.h2: Which appraisal district and county handle my Cedar Park property taxes?
sections.html:
Read your latest tax statement: it names the county and appraisal district that carry your parcel. Cedar Park describes itself as part of Williamson County, and the Williamson Central Appraisal District values property there.

Texas levies no state property tax, so each local unit sets its own rate. Values are fixed as of January 1, a lien for that year attaches the same day, and bills follow in October. The Comptroller says unpaid tax is delinquent on February 1, when a penalty and interest begin to build.

Skip online estimators for rates. Ask the Williamson County tax office for the adopted rate of each unit on your bill, and ask the title company how the year's bill will be split with the buyer.

sections.h2: How do the homestead exemption and the 10 percent cap work in Cedar Park?
sections.html:
The cap keeps the assessed value of a lived-in home from jumping, and it stays with the owner rather than the house. Williamson CAD says a home qualifies in the second full year the exemption has been on the property for the same owner, and that increases in existing assessed value are held to 10 percent a year even when market value climbs faster.

The district also says the cap does not transfer with ownership, so a buyer starts fresh and may see a bigger jump than you did. Useful points from the district:

  • You apply once; the exemption stays unless you move or add another one.
  • A Texas driver license or ID showing your current address is required.
  • Processing can take up to 90 days.
  • The chief appraiser reviews every homestead exemption at least once every five tax years.

sections.h2: What does Cedar Park's short-term rental registration mean for sellers?
sections.html:
If your Cedar Park house is rented for stays of 30 consecutive days or fewer, City Council's April 2026 ordinance applies. Registration became required on October 1, 2026, costs $100 a year, and ties into Hotel Occupancy Tax reporting under Chapter 10 of the City Code. The city estimates about 200 active short-term rentals.

A buyer who wants to keep renting will ask whether the registration exists and whether tax was remitted. The city lists Development Services at 512-401-5100 for registration and Utility Billing at 512-401-5300 for hotel tax payments, and registered owners can watch remittance through an online portal. Gather those records before you list.

sections.h2: What permit and repair rules should I check before selling in Cedar Park?
sections.html:
Open permits are a common reason a Cedar Park closing pauses. The city runs permits through the MGO Connect portal, and Development Services is at the City Hall campus, 450 Cypress Creek Road, Building 1. Its zoning map tool, CPAtlas, lets you type in an address to see zoning.

sections.h2: What if the Cedar Park house is inherited, in foreclosure or has a tenant?
sections.html:
Each situation runs on a Texas clock, so start early.

  • Foreclosure: a borrower may reinstate within 20 days of receiving the default notice, and the sale notice must go out at least three weeks ahead of an auction held at the courthouse on a first Tuesday.
  • Inheritance: heirs have four years to probate a will; a muniment of title can move property without full administration, and the small estate affidavit tops out at $75,000 excluding homestead and exempt property.
  • Tenant: expect at least a 3-day written notice to vacate before a justice court filing, unless the lease says otherwise.

A cash buyer can take a house with these issues, but the title company still needs proof of authority to sell. A Williamson County probate attorney can say which paper fits.

sections.h2: What should I do first if I want to sell my Cedar Park house quickly?
sections.html:
Five checks give you your real options within days.

  • Pull the tax statement and confirm the district and any balance.
  • Ask Development Services whether any permit on the address is open.
  • Get your mortgage payoff figure.
  • If the house was a short-term rental, collect registration and hotel tax records.
  • Name your deadline, such as a sale date or a move.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Cedar Park house with an open building permit?
faqs.a: Yes, but it complicates the sale. A Cedar Park permit lapses if work does not begin, or stops, for 180 days. Ask Development Services at 512-401-5100 to review the status, or sell as-is to a buyer who accepts the open item.

faqs.q: Do I need to register my Cedar Park short-term rental before selling?
faqs.a: If guests stay 30 days or fewer, registration has been required since October 1, 2026 at $100 a year. Buyers who plan to keep renting will ask for the registration and your hotel occupancy tax records.

faqs.q: Does my homestead tax cap pass to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. Williamson CAD states the cap does not transfer with ownership. The new owner applies for an exemption of their own, and the cap counts from their first full year.

faqs.q: When do Texas property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: Tax unpaid after January 31 is delinquent on February 1, per the Texas Comptroller. Ask the Williamson County tax office for your exact balance.

faqs.q: How is a foreclosure sale scheduled in Texas?
faqs.a: At the courthouse on a first Tuesday, between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m., after a sale notice of at least 21 days. The borrower may reinstate within 20 days of the default notice.
